subject: Literature
title: Lolita and the Boundaries of Art
description: A 60-second lesson on Lolita and the Boundaries of Art.

hook.text: Vladimir Nabokov's Lolita was rejected by every American publisher and first published by a Paris erotica press.

buildup.text: The novel is narrated by a predator who uses beautiful prose to justify his crimes against a twelve-year-old girl.

discovery.text: Nabokov designed the novel to expose how eloquent language can disguise monstrous behavior and seduce readers.

twist.text: France banned its own publication of the book, and Britain and several other countries followed shortly after.

climax.text: Lolita forced literature to confront the question of whether artistic brilliance can coexist with repulsive content.

punchline.text: The most beautiful prose in English describes the ugliest crime.

quiz.question: What was Nabokov's purpose in using beautiful prose for a monstrous narrator?
options: To expose how eloquent language can disguise and justify monstrous behavior
He had no deeper purpose beyond entertainment
